heroHeadline: NASA MOON BASE CONTRACTS: ~$1B AWARDED TO ASTROLAB, LUNAR OUTPOST, BLUE ORIGIN, FIREFLY — MOON BASE I TO SHACKLETON RIDGE TARGETING FALL 2026; ARTEMIS III CREW REVEAL JUNE 9
heroSubtitle: May 26: NASA's Moon Base news conference unveiled nearly $1 billion in initial contracts: Astrolab ($219M CLV-1 crewed lunar rover), Lunar Outpost ($220M Pegasus LTV), Blue Origin ($188M Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance cargo lander to deliver both rovers to the lunar south pole), and Firefly Aerospace (MoonFall hopping drones from Elytra Dark spacecraft at 50 km orbit). Moon Base I — Blue Origin Blue Moon Endurance to Shackleton Connecting Ridge — is targeting no later than fall 2026, making it the first hardware delivery to the Moon Base site. Moon Base II (Astrobotic Griffin + Astrolab FLIP rover, 1,100+ lbs) follows later in 2026. Artemis IV (first crewed lunar landing) remains on track for early 2028; a permanent nuclear-powered base is the 2036 goal. The $20–30B, 7–11 year architecture was announced by Administrator Jared Isaacman, Associate Administrator Lori Glaze (Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate), and Moon Base Program Manager Carlos García-Galán. Separately, NASA confirmed the Artemis III crew will be announced June 9, 2026 at 11 a.m. EDT at Johnson Space Center (live on NASA+) — the first astronaut names attached to the redesigned mission (LEO rendezvous and docking test targeting late 2027 using a structural spacer instead of ICPS). The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 47 post-splashdown at JSC continuing reconditioning. On the SpaceX front, the FAA's IFT-12 mishap investigation (Booster 19 boostback failure, May 22) continues; IFT-13 (Ship 40 + Booster 20, FCC window May 29–Nov 29) cannot launch until the assessment concludes — earliest Q3 2026.
